title: panel: toggle cutout is 6.5mm, real sub-mini toggles need 4.95mm
description:
Found while sourcing the RANGE switch for the slew limiter.

TOGGLE_MM = 6.5 (panel.rs:120) drives ControlKind::Switch cutouts. The Dailywell DW5 sub-mini toggle Thonk sells (2MD6T1B1M2QES) specifies a panel hole of:

  diameter  4.95mm  (0.195in)
  with a flat at 4.55mm (0.179in) for anti-rotation
  bushing thread 10-48 UNS-2A

So our hole is 1.55mm oversized. A switch in a hole that loose sits crooked and the nut has to do all the work -- and the D-flat that stops it rotating is missing entirely, so it WILL rotate in use.

FIX: TOGGLE_MM -> 4.95, and consider a D-shaped cutout (CutoutShape has RoundedRect; a circle-with-flat is a new shape, or approximate). Check the Alpha/other toggles Thonk sells before settling on one number -- the DWB "mini" range is a different size to the DW "sub-mini" range, so the vocabulary may need both.

Same class of error as [[legion-of-bom-3s8]] (1U hole inset unverified): panel geometry taken from a plausible number rather than a datasheet.
notes:
REFRAMED after sourcing two real candidates. There is no single correct number -- the hole follows the part:

  Dailywell 2MD6T1B1M2QES (Thonk DW5)   4.95mm dia + 4.55mm flat, 10-48 UNS bushing
  E-Switch 100DP6T1B1M1QEH               6.35mm dia, 1/4-40 bushing

Our TOGGLE_MM = 6.5 is badly wrong for the Dailywell (1.55mm oversize) and very nearly right for the E-Switch (0.15mm over). So the bug is not "6.5 is the wrong constant", it is "a single constant cannot be right" -- BuiltinCutouts needs per-part cutout geometry keyed off the MPN, which is what CutoutSource::cutout(mpn, footprint) already takes an mpn for but never uses.

That also makes this a parts-library question: the cutout dimensions belong WITH the part, same standing rule as [[legion-of-bom-okm]]. Until then, at minimum add a second toggle entry so both bushing sizes are expressible.

Anti-rotation flat: the Dailywell needs a D-shaped hole. CutoutShape has no such variant.

title: pot swap to RV9012NO-PA25B7.0: value and footprint both change
description:
User picked RV9012NO-PA25B7.0 for the attenuverter pot, from the SuperSynthesis fab packages. Two things to settle before swapping, because neither is a like-for-like substitution:

1. VALUE. The SuperSynthesis BOMs describe it as "Tall Trimmer 10k". RV2 is currently 100k, and the circuit comment says why: "high enough not to load the CV source". A 10k pot across a CV input is a 10k load, which will sag another modules output. If the swap goes ahead at 10k that is a deliberate loading choice, not a detail.

2. FOOTPRINT. RV1/RV2 are on Potentiometer_THT:Potentiometer_Alpha_RD901F-40-00D_Single_Vertical. RV9012 is a different body and pinout, so this changes the board footprint AND the panel cutout envelope (BuiltinCutouts Alpha9mm), which feeds min_panel_hp and every derived panel.

3. It is listed against R-designators under JLC assembly in 2opfm/eg/tvca, which is what a trimmer looks like in a BOM, not a panel control. Worth confirming this is really the panel pot SuperSynthesis fit rather than their onboard trim.

Where the MPN goes: slew_limiter.py Part() carries no mpn field today, so this needs either the SKiDL part to declare one or a parts-library record -- the latter matches the standing rule that a components data travels with the component. See [[legion-of-bom-okm]].
notes:
VALUE CONCERN WITHDRAWN. Asked whether 10k works with the op-amp attenuverter: yes, and it is the better choice.

In the passive circuit the wiper feeds R5 directly, so the pots own output impedance (up to R/4 = 25k at mid-rotation for 100k) sits in series with R5 and makes CV depth interact with knob position -- which is why 100k was chosen. In the op-amp topology the wiper drives a high-Z non-inverting input, so that interaction vanishes and the op-amp output drives R5 stiffly. Depth becomes linear.

Gain is set by the two resistors, not the pot: Vout = W(1 + R2/R1) - CV(R2/R1), and with R1 = R2 that is 2W - CV, sweeping -CV / 0 / +CV. Pot value is independent of them. 10k gives lower Johnson noise and less leakage sensitivity than 100k.

Only consequence is a 10k load on the patched CV source, which any buffered Eurorack output drives without trouble.

STILL OPEN on this bead: whether RV9012NO-PA25B7.0 is a panel control at all (listed as a trimmer against R-designators under JLC assembly) and the footprint/cutout change. Those are mechanical, not electrical.

title: lob panel derive: width from minimum_hp but positions from the built board
description:
Found while checking the new panel art on puget slew_limiter.

`lob panel derive slew_limiter.py` prints:
  auto width: minimum 5 HP
  from the built board (out/slew_limiter/slew_limiter.kicad_pcb) - 5 cutout(s) at their real positions

It takes the WIDTH from minimum_hp (5 HP) and the POSITIONS from a board that was laid out against an 8 HP panel. The two disagree, and the result has overlapping hardware: RV2 lands at y=73.9 and J1 at y=67.0, 6.9mm apart, where a 9mm pot needs ~14mm and a jack ~9mm. Rendered the panel PCB and the IN jack sits inside the CV AMT pot cutout.

Either the width should come from the board too (it is the master, per bjd), or positions should be re-derived when the width changes. Silently mixing the two produces a spec that cannot be built.

Repro: cd puget-hardware && lob panel derive slew_limiter.py, then lob panel pcb on the result and look at it.
close_reason:
Fixed, but the filed diagnosis was wrong on both counts. The board IS 5.00 HP so width and positions agreed, and the 6.9mm reading was pin-1-to-jack rather than shaft-to-jack.

REAL FAULT: guide::parse_board documents cx/cy as "board-space centre" and sets them to the footprint ORIGIN. An Alpha pots origin is pin 1, so panel_from_board drilled pot holes off the shaft -- RV1/RV2 landed at x=10.2 on a panel whose jacks were at 12.7, i.e. 2.5mm left of centre. And the reverse path (cutout -> placement) already subtracts the offset, so board -> panel -> board drifted a part by one offset per trip. The round-trip test passed because both ends were consistently wrong.

panel_from_board now maps the courtyard bbox centre. Re-derived on puget slew_limiter: all cutouts centre on 12.7, spacing 20 / 18.4 / 16 / 16mm, panel PCB renders with no overlapping holes.

ALSO LANDED: Rule::Separation (panel hardware judged on panel envelopes, Physical tier), and Placer::anchored() + legalize_pinning so legalization can never slide a panel control off its cutout -- it reports instead. Tests for both.

title: IC pin names: KiCad leaves the most useful ones unnamed (IABC, OUT)
description:
Fallout from sto. The schematic now shows every pin name KiCad declares, but KiCad declares fewer than the bead assumed.

Ground truth, read from Amplifier_Operational.kicad_sym: LM13700 names pins 2/15 DIODE_BIAS, 3/14 +, 4/13 -, 6 V-, 11 V+. Pins 1, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 16 are named ~ (KiCad explicit no-name).

So the two pins stos headline example wanted are the two we cannot get: pin 1 IABC (the bias input the RATE pot drives) and pin 5 (the OTA output). On slew_limiter U1 now reads 3 +, 4 -, and 1 / 5 / 7 / 8 stay bare. Half the topology is legible, the interesting half is not.

The names exist in the datasheet, not the symbol, so the source has to be a parts library carrying verified pinouts per MPN -- which is the Dolt parts library seam, and matches the standing rule that a components data travels WITH the component rather than being special-cased. See [[legion-of-bom-okm]].

WORK: resolve pin function names through the parts library, falling back to the KiCad symbol. Then a boxed IC can read 1 IABC / 5 OUT.

title: harness: examples/board_preview is unrepresentative for DRC-level conclusions
description:
It derives its own panel with derive_panel, which stacks every control in one idealised centred column. Its boards carry ~69 DRC errors (24 tracks_crossing, 25 unconnected_items, 13 solder_mask_bridge) where the SHIPPED slew_limiter board carries 5, all unconnected_items.

So it is fine for placement-level A/B against itself — same harness before and after a change — and useless for judging whether a board is buildable or how many DRC errors a width really has. It has now misled me twice: once by passing no anchors at all (fixed), and once by making 4 HP vs 5 HP DRC comparisons look meaningful when the router was flailing at both widths for unrelated reasons.

FIX: build the harness against a real declared panel spec. slew_limiter's lives in the circuits repo, not here, so this probably means either checking in a representative panel spec as a fixture or pointing the harness at a circuits-repo path. Until then, put a warning at the top of the example saying what it is and is not good for.
close_reason:
Fixed. Three things were wrong, in increasing order of impact:

1. It passed no anchors (fixed earlier).
2. It derived its own idealised panel. Now it builds against a real declared spec, defaulting to examples/fixtures/slew_limiter_panel.toml, captured off the SHIPPED board via the new panel_from_pcb example. That revealed the shipped board is 8 HP -- every 4 vs 5 HP DRC comparison I had been drawing was at a width nothing ships at.
3. It overrode the router with MstRouter. BoardOptions::new defaults to GridRouter and the CLI never overrides it, so the harness was measuring a router that ships nowhere. This was most of the gap: 16 tracks_crossing and 25 unconnected_items were the MST connector, not placement.

Harness now reports DRC: 0 errors, against the shipped board 5. It is representative and can be trusted for DRC-level conclusions -- which unblocks t5t (minimum_hp routability), the whole point of the bead.

title: rules: the decoupling rule measures distance, but the objective is loop inductance
notes:
FIRST SLICE DONE (commit f35644b): the rule now names itself a proxy. DECOUPLE_GAP_MM's docs state the objective is loop inductance and that distance is a stand-in, with an explicit 'do not tighten this number expecting better decoupling'; the rule's own 'why' text says the same, so it reaches the guide and the dashboard panel. The rules module doc generalises it — every electrical rule will have this gap between what a placement can see and what matters, and each should name its proxy.

The two better versions remain open, unchanged: cap-to-POWER-PIN rather than cap-to-centre (blocked on per-pad net in PartFacts), and true loop area (needs the routed board, probably not worth it).
PARTLY ADDRESSED by legion-of-bom-22c: crate::decouple::snap now PLACES each bypass cap against the power pin it bypasses (pad-to-pin 10.0mm -> 4.5mm on slew_limiter), so the physical objective is met by construction rather than by scoring.

What remains here is exactly the framing this bead was filed for: the RULE still measures cap-centre to IC-centre. It now passes comfortably, which is worse than failing -- a regression in the snap pass would hide behind a green rule. Making Proximity measure pad-to-pin (PartFacts::pin_offsets now carries the geometry needed) changes thresholds and the layout loop scoring, so it was deliberately not bundled into the fix.

title: Imported BOMs without part numbers: suggest MPNs from value + package
description:
Measured across the five SuperSynthesis packages: only 2OPFM fills its distributor column (20/24 lines). PHRSR, SCANNER, TVCA and EG leave it blank entirely, so their BOMs cannot be priced or ordered as imported — 20, 15, 16 and 32 lines respectively with nothing to look up.

Everything needed already exists: [[legion-of-bom-lrr]] built suggest_mpns(part) which turns value + footprint into ranked candidates via Mouser keyword search, and an imported BOM line carries exactly that (value "10uF 50v", footprint "CAP_1206"). So: for an imported circuit with blank part numbers, run the same suggestion path, and — per the okm human-verification gate — SUGGEST rather than assign. Surface candidates in the Visual BOM so the builder confirms one, and write the confirmed choice back to the package or a sidecar.

Package strings need a little normalising first: these are "0603 CAP", "CAP_1206", "SOD-323", not clean footprint names — import::package_size_mm and package_is_through_hole already read them, so the same vocabulary can feed the query builder. Follows [[legion-of-bom-u7p]].
notes:
CLI SHIPPED: lob import repair <package> [--search] [--limit N]. core/bom_repair.rs classifies the comment column into Mpn / Value / Label, which is the crux — the column does three jobs at once. Ordering rules earned against real data: (1) FIRST TOKEN decides (authors append ratings/tolerance/notes: '10uF 50v', '10k 0603 1%'); (2) value tested BEFORE mpn ('10uF' satisfies both heuristics, only one is true); (3) mpn tested BEFORE the connector rule (else a jack with a real MPN, WQP-WQP518MA, is thrown away as a signal label). Wrong order gave 28/111 unsourceable; right order gives 12, and those 12 genuinely are (DNP + jacks named CV/OUT/TRIG). Across the 5 packages: 63 lines carry an MPN in the comment, 36 are searchable, 12 not. PHRSR alone: 0 -> 12 recovered outright (STM32F334K8, TL072D, AMS1117-3.3, 1N4148WS, WQP-WQP518MA...) + 8 searchable. sourcing::suggest_by_keyword added so an imported line can reuse the lrr search without a Part. 10 unit tests. Gates: 253 core + 11 web, fmt/clippy clean.

HONEST LIMIT — the --search path is wired and returns results, but the RESULTS ARE POOR for generic passives: '10uF capacitor 1206' returns Visaton speaker caps, '100k resistor 0603' returns MOX power resistors, all 0 stock. This is the keyword-noise limitation lrr already documented; it needs the value-parse tightening noted there (compare parsed ohms/farads against each candidate, and filter by package) before it is trustworthy. Comment RECOVERY is solid and is where the value is today.

NOT DONE: (a) no UI surface — the user asked for UI and CLI; the dashboard BOM does not yet show recovered/suggested MPNs or let you confirm one; (b) nothing writes the confirmed MPN back to the package or a sidecar; (c) the okm verification gate is not applied to a recovered number.

title: THT drill clearance: are footprint drills big enough for the real part?
description:
User: "I do not think the pot holes (not the pins) but the holders are drilled big enough."

WHAT I VERIFIED (so this is not the pipeline): our gerbers faithfully reproduce the KiCad footprint. Potentiometer_Alpha_RD901F-40-00D_Single_Vertical declares the two mounting lugs as (drill oval 1.1 1.8) and pins 1-3 as (drill 1). Our Excellon emits exactly that: tool T3 = 1.1mm routed 0.7mm via G85, giving a 1.1 x 1.8mm slot, four of them (2 pots x 2 lugs). Nothing is dropped or shrunk.

SO THE QUESTION IS UPSTREAM: is the KiCad footprint tight for the physical Alpha 9mm pot? Needs a caliper on the real part (lug cross-section) and on a fab-house sample, which is exactly the verified mechanical data the parts library is meant to carry — see [[legion-of-bom-okm]].

LIKELY REAL FIX, once measured, is a DFM rule rather than a per-footprint edit: a drill-oversize allowance on through-hole pads (fab houses typically want lead diameter + 0.2-0.3mm, and plating shrinks a hole further). That belongs in the declarative rule work [[legion-of-bom-avg]] as a physical-tier constraint, applied at fab export so it cannot be forgotten, and reported so the builder sees what was widened and why. Also worth a DFM check that no slot is below the house minimum. Related: [[legion-of-bom-j54.7]].

title: Eagle import (.brd/.sch) — Mutable Instruments and friends
description:
User: "Maybe eagle_brd from Mutables." Eagle is a much better import target than DipTrace: since v6 .brd/.sch are XML with a published DTD, so components, nets, footprints and placement are all directly readable — meaning a real netlist, and therefore schematic view, ERC and simulation, not just layout re-use.

TWO ROUTES: (a) parse the XML ourselves into the Circuit model — no new dependency, full control, and it fits the CircuitSource seam; (b) shell out to KiCad, which ships an Eagle importer, then read the resulting .kicad_pcb/.kicad_sch with the parsers we already have. (b) is less code and reuses proven conversion, but adds a kicad-cli dependency for import and must degrade gracefully when absent.

Mutable Instruments hardware is open (cc-by-sa) and Eagle-based, so this unlocks a well-known body of designs. Distinct from [[legion-of-bom-u7p]] (fab-package import, layout only, no nets).
notes: SHIPPED (first slice): lob import eagle <sch> [--board <brd>] [--skidl <out>]. core/eagle.rs — hand-rolled XML scanner (handles '>' inside quoted attrs), parse_schematic -> real Circuit with nets from <net>/<segment>/<pinref>, parts from <part> resolved to a package via the file's own library/deviceset/device chain; parse_board -> EaglePlacement (x/y/rot, 'MR90' = mirrored to back); to_skidl -> a runnable-looking SKiDL script so an import becomes an editable definition. Judgement calls: (1) schematic symbols with no package (frames, GND/supply markers) are NOT components — skipped, counted, and their pins excluded since a GND symbol's pin IS the net; (2) unknown packages pass through as 'eagle:<name>' and are reported, never guessed — but AMBIGUOUS ones (Eagle names passives by bare size, '0603') are settled by the refdes, since R14/C9 say what the package doesn't. VERIFIED on Mutable Instruments: grids 106 parts/70 nets/108 placements, peaks 90/69, ripples 105/63, tides 139/98; generated SKiDL for grids is 514 lines with real per-pin nets. Gates: 238 core + 11 web, fmt/clippy clean, 5 unit tests. NOT DONE: (a) symbol library is GUESSED from refdes prefix (Device:R/C/L/D/Q, else REVIEW_ME) — Eagle records the package, not the KiCad schematic symbol, so generated Part() lines need review; (b) 17 unmapped packages on grids alone (HC49UP, LQFP48, ALPS_POT_VERTICAL_PS, SOIC16N...) — the footprint map covers common passives/SOT/SOIC only; (c) placements parsed but not yet fed into a board, so 'import to layout' is read-only; (d) no manifest integration — an Eagle circuit cannot yet be declared in lob.toml the way [[legion-of-bom-u7p]] fab packages can; (e) multi-sheet schematics untested.

title: Schematic: split multi-unit symbols (op-amps) into their units

title: Schematic: draw real KiCad component symbols instead of boxes
description:
User: "why cannot we get kicad component symbols?" Answer: we can — the current box rendering was a shortcut, not a limitation. Everything needed is already present and verified:
- Part.library_part is already parsed from the netlist libsource, e.g. (libsource (lib "Device") (part "C")) -> "Device:C" (crates/core/src/netlist.rs).
- 223 .kicad_sym libraries are installed and we ALREADY read them: crates/core/src/symbols.rs resolves SPICE models out of them and skidl::kicad_symbol_dir() locates the dir.
- Symbol bodies carry real graphic primitives — rectangle / polyline / circle / arc with stroke and fill, in mm (e.g. Device:R body unit R_0_1 is a rectangle -1.016,-2.54 to 1.016,2.54).
- Pins carry position, angle, length, number and name: (pin passive line (at 0 3.81 270) (length 1.27)) — so wires can terminate at REAL pins instead of the box edge, which also improves the routing.
- crates/core/src/sexpr.rs already parses this format.

WORK:
1. Resolve the symbol: library_part -> <lib>.kicad_sym -> symbol block, following (extends "...") inheritance (verified: TL072 extends LM2904).
2. Emit body primitives as SVG. KiCad symbol space is mm with Y up; the sheet is Y down, so flip. Honour stroke width and fill type.
3. Anchor net wires at real pin endpoints (pin at + angle + length gives the wire attach point) instead of the box edge.
4. Cache parsed symbols per (lib, part) — a circuit reuses the same few.
5. Fall back to the current box when the symbol or the symbol dir is missing (KiCad may not be installed) — same graceful-degradation rule as every other external dependency here.

HARD PART — multi-unit symbols: LM2904 has sub-units LM2904_1_1, _2_1, _3_1 (two op-amps plus the power unit) but the netlist has ONE component U2 for the whole chip. A real schematic places unit A and unit B separately, each wired to its own nets, with power drawn once. So pins must be grouped by unit and each unit placed as its own graphical instance — real schematic-capture logic. Passives/diodes/jacks/pots/headers are single-unit and straightforward; do those first and let multi-unit parts fall back to a box until the unit splitting lands. Follows [[legion-of-bom-agr]].
close_reason: Real KiCad symbols now drawn in the schematic view. symbols::read_symbol_graphics() parses a symbol body (rectangle/polyline/circle/arc) + pins from <lib>.kicad_sym, follows (extends) inheritance (TL072 -> LM2904), and reports unit count; resolved from Part.library_part which the netlist parser already recorded, cached per lib:part. Wires now attach at the REAL pin tip (the netlist names the pin per connection) instead of a box edge. KiCad's three fill modes modelled as SymFill — outline=solid ink, background=sheet colour (occludes without going black), none=open; collapsing them to a bool had rendered audio jacks as black blobs. Verified on puget slew_limiter: 12/14 parts as real symbols (resistor rectangles, cap plates, pot wiper arrows, jack switched-tip contacts), U1/U2 boxed. Gates: 217 core + 11 web, fmt/clippy clean; 4 offline tests using synthetic .kicad_sym fixtures (fill modes, extends, multi-unit, missing lib). DEFERRED: multi-unit parts (op-amps) still fall back to a box — drawing them means splitting pins across separately-placed units, real schematic-capture work; also no symbol rotation/mirroring for tidier wiring, and no pin-name labels.

title: Orientation-aware anchored placement: rotate controls + align mount point to cutout
description: EurorackPlacer::place (board.rs) places every part at rotation_deg=0.0 and puts the footprint ORIGIN at the cutout center. Two bugs: (1) POTS render 90-deg wrong (Alpha9mm native orientation = pins in a horizontal row → landscape); anchored controls need a rotation so pins face INTO the board. (2) JACKS don't line up with panel holes: the panel-mount point (jack barrel / pot bushing center) isn't the footprint origin, and nothing offsets for it — align the mechanical mount point to the cutout, not the origin. Needs per-control orientation + mount-point-offset data (extend BuiltinCutouts/CutoutSpec or PartFacts). Verify by regenerating slew_limiter board+panel and checking barrel↔hole concentricity.

FIX: align the mount point (PartFacts.origin_offset ≈ courtyard centre ≈ shaft/barrel) to the cutout — place the footprint origin at cutout - rotate_offset(offset, rot), keep-out re-centred on the cutout. VERIFIED on slew_limiter: RV1/RV2 origins shifted to x=9.9 so shafts land at x=15.2 (panel hole); jacks' y-offset applied so barrels hit the holes. (2) Sub-board courtyard = per-header-row rects (general from spec.rows), not the full body, so KiCad stops false-flagging same-side parts in the open centre. Nothing Daisy-hardcoded (driven by pad layers + standoff + rows). comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
Attempted naive packing (let a short part's placement overlap the sub-board's courtyard via a height-aware nearest_clear_spot). REVERTED — it is not DRC-clean, for two reasons found via real KiCad DRC on a Daisy 8HP panel demo (Daisy + 12 short 0603 parts netted to it):

1) Parts land ON the sub-board's header pads → clearance / shorting_items / pth_inside_courtyard (the header pins are real copper on the main board). Needs PAD-AWARE placement: the sub-board's header-pad regions must stay hard keep-outs while only the clear interior is soft.

2) MORE fundamental: KiCad courtyards_overlap fires on ANY 2D courtyard overlap regardless of Z clearance. So even perfect pad-aware placement (parts in the clear centre strip) still trips 9x courtyards_overlap against the Daisy body courtyard. To be DRC-clean the sub-board's COURTYARD must be modelled to exclude the usable under-space (courtyard = header/pad regions only, not the full 18x51 body).

Measured: naive packing = 25 DRC errors (9 courtyards_overlap, 4 pth_inside_courtyard, clearance/shorting on header pins, silk). Same board with parts placed AROUND the Daisy (no packing) = 0 errors, 0 unconnected.

Re-scope: (a) sub-board courtyard covers only its pads/edges (not the body interior) + (b) pad-aware placement. Both required. PartFacts already has the height data path from 25z.4. Not started beyond this investigation.

Daisy demo + slew limiter: 0 false collisions, still DRC-clean. title: Ground pour fragments around a sub-board's dense THT header grid -> starved_thermal
description: A sub-board's header (e.g. Daisy's 40 THT pads) punches a dense grid of holes through the ground pour, splitting it into islands; a GND pad's thermal spokes then land on an isolated island (KiCad starved_thermal). Seen on the daisy_demo board (1 error: pad 20 [GND] of A1, B.Cu island). Inherent to placing dense THT headers on a poured board. Fix options: stitching vias between F/B pours near the header, or pour-aware GND pad handling. Relates to j54.17 (back-side pour). Not a footprint defect (footprint places+routes clean).
close_reason: ground_stitching_vias places a GND via just off each through-hole ground pad, tying the F.Cu/B.Cu pours together locally so a pour island fenced off by a dense THT header grid reconnects to the intact pour on the other layer. Placed inside the board edge and clear of all other-net copper (pads/tracks/vias); a boxed-in pad is skipped, not forced. Daisy demo: 1 starved_thermal -> 0 DRC errors (1 stitch added). 8HP slew limiter unchanged: 0 errors (7 stitches added, improves the ground plane). 2 unit tests + 137 total, clippy/fmt clean.

title: 4HP: back-side SOIC U2 adjacent pads short on B.Cu (real narrow-module blocker, NOT a space issue)
description: Reframes 3jh: at 4HP the slew limiter's DRC errors are NOT physical infeasibility (14x128mm 3U has ample area to stack parts vertically). They cluster on ONE part: U2, a back-side SOIC on B.Cu, whose adjacent pads short (pads 2-3,3-4,5-6,7-8: shorting_items + solder_mask_bridge, different nets). Likely the B.Cu ground pour / routing interacting with the fine-pitch (1.27mm) SOIC after the back-flip. Fixing this (plus better vertical stacking) should make single-board narrow modules route clean, per user: rotate/stack in the tall 3U rather than pack horizontally. Found while scoping 3jh.
notes: ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED (2026-07-24): NOT the B.Cu ground pour (ruled out — the shorts persist with the pour disabled) and NOT a neighbor overlap (nothing within 4mm of U2). It's the free-part 90° ROTATION of the fine-pitch back-side SOIC: at 5HP U2 is rot=0 (clean); at 4HP the placer rotates it to fit width → its rotated pads trip shorting_items + rear solder_mask_bridge on EVERY adjacent pad pair (2-3,3-4,5-6,7-8), even though geometrically the pads sit 0.67mm apart (0.6mm pad, 1.27mm pitch). Confirmed: disabling the rotation of SMD parts eliminates all shorts+mask_bridges. PARTIAL FIX LANDED: SeededPlacer's free-part rotation now only turns THROUGH-HOLE parts portrait, never fine-pitch SMD ICs (also correct practice — rotating a SOIC hurts fanout). This makes the default DRC-clean (5HP, consistent) and removes the +1-HP routability band-aid I'd added. REMAINING (the actual 4HP goal): a SOIC unrotated is too wide to fit 4HP, so the module can't go below 5HP. To reach 4HP we must make the ROTATED back SOIC route clean — i.e. understand WHY rotated pads 0.67mm apart read as shorting (likely the rotated+mirrored back-footprint pad/mask emission in board.rs vs KiCad). That's the open work here.

title: Placement: free parts land within edge clearance of the board edge on narrow HP (unroutable + copper_edge_clearance)
description: Surfaced by j54.23: on a 6HP slew-limiter variant the CV jack J4 (a free/auto-placed part, not a panel cutout) is placed hard against the board edge — its GND PTH pad trips copper_edge_clearance and 3 nets to J4 are left unrouted because the router (correctly, post-j54.23) won't route into the edge band to reach it. The placer must keep every part's courtyard an edge-clearance (~0.5mm) inside the board outline. Pre-existing (the pad-edge error predates j54.23; that fix just unmasked the unroutable connections). Related to 3jh (dense narrow modules). The real 8HP board is unaffected (0 errors).
close_reason: overflow_drop() stacks unfittable free parts in an off-board lane 2mm below the bottom edge instead of straddling it at y1+2 (~1mm inside), so an overflowed part no longer trips copper_edge_clearance — the failure surfaces honestly as unrouted nets. Fixed in both SeededPlacer and EurorackPlacer. 8HP slew limiter unchanged (0 DRC errors); 6HP CV jack J4 drops 3.9mm below the edge, 3 nets unconnected (J4 unfittable on 30mm = 3jh, not this bug). Regression test overflow_parts_drop_clear_below_the_board_edge; 131 tests, clippy/fmt clean.

title: Dense narrow modules (<=4HP): controls eat the board -> offset-column or 2-board stack
description: At 4HP a centered jack/pot courtyard (~13mm) spans nearly the whole 14mm usable width, so anchored panel controls leave no room for components on the same PCB (103 DRC errors even SMD+double-sided). Real fix is architectural: (a) offset the control column to one side to clear a component strip, or (b) a 2-board stack (controls PCB + main PCB + board-to-board header). Neither exists yet; needed for auto-layout of dense <=4HP modules.

title: Router: rip-up-and-retry to resolve the last unrouted nets (8HP=4, 6HP=6 left)
description: With A* fast enough to iterate, the remaining gap to clean boards is the router giving up on nets blocked by already-committed copper. Add rip-up: when a net can't route, rip up the blocking net(s) and re-route in a better order. DESIGN 6.5 names this as the loop's job. Would take 8HP/6HP from ~10-13 errors toward clean.
close_reason: Rip-up-and-reroute landed: route_pass reports blame (nets whose committed copper boxes in an unreachable pad); route() forces those blockers to route after the victim via accumulating ordering constraints + topo-sort (cycles dropped). Combined with A* + a conservative rotation heuristic (only rotate parts too wide for the board), the CV-added SMD PCBA slew limiter now routes 6HP AND 8HP fully DRC-clean (0 errors, was 10-13). 4HP 103->46 (still architectural, see 3jh). 128 tests pass.

title: Panel mounting holes: oval (slotted) vs round option + placement pattern (diagonal L/R 2-hole, or all 4)
description: Eurorack panels use oval/slotted mounting holes so horizontal position adjusts in the rack. Add: hole shape (oval slot | round) and placement pattern (diagonal top-left+bottom-right 2-hole | all 4 | left 2). Wire into panel spec TOML + PCB Edge.Cuts + DXF rendering. Real-Eurorack default: oval, diagonal.

title: Layout: HP-minimizing mode — find the smallest HP the module fits in (controls + board)
description: A mode where layout optimizes for minimum HP: try successively narrower HP widths, place+route the board and fit the panel controls, pick the smallest HP where everything fits without overflow/unroutable criticals. Ties into derive-panel (auto-choose HP) and the iterative layout loop (j54.6).
notes: UPDATE: the +1-HP routability band-aid noted earlier is REMOVED. It was compensating for the j54.25 rotation-short (place-min 4 with a rotated SOIC didn't route). With j54.25's partial fix (SMD ICs no longer rotate), place-min=5 for slew_limiter ROUTES DRC-clean, so minimum_hp now honestly returns place-min (no buffer) → default 5HP clean. True route-aware sizing (route+DRC per candidate) still the real thing for the general case.

Tagging SLEW_NODE (high-Z OTA feedback) and the output path would (a) protect them in placement and (b) recover the SIG_OUT regression (16->30mm) seen when U2 pulled toward its higher-fanout neighbours. One-line change per net in the separate ~/src/puget-hardware repo.

Verified end-to-end: netlist emits (class 'Default,Critical'); is_critical() now parses comma-joined classes; analog loop reports critical 53mm and drives SLEW_NODE 86->8.6mm, SIG_IN 32->14mm. DRC-clean. Fab regenerated.

description: lob run's simulate stage hardcodes an ngspice AC sweep on nets named IN/OUT. The slew limiter needs TRANSIENT analysis (slew-rate response to a step), and uses SIG_IN/SIG_OUT. Predicted in slew-limiter-circuit.md ('first circuit where ngspice checks behavior over time... transient, not AC sweep'). Add a transient sim path + configurable stimulus/probe nets so lob run works on time-domain circuits. Maps to tus.3.

Validated end-to-end on an RC step response (ngspice). Slew-limiter values (R3=47k, C1=47nF) confirmed via a datasheet-behavioural OTA core: 10.23 V/ms = IABC/C1, 10V in ~1ms. Full LM13700-part pipeline run still needs the cited SPICE model (okm.9).

title: GridRouter leaves nets unrouted on denser boards (slew limiter: SIG_IN->U2.3)
description: The slew limiter (11 parts, 2-layer) left 1 net unrouted (SIG_IN to U2 pin 3). The maze router's completion rate drops on denser real boards vs the trivial Phase 0 demos. Needs ripup-and-retry / ordering heuristics / more layers, or at least a clear manual-route handoff. Feeds the iterative-layout loop (j54).
close_reason: Added rip-up-free retry to GridRouter: failed nets get grid priority on the next pass so their blockers reroute around them (route_pass + priority loop, <=6 rounds, deterministic). Slew limiter SIG_IN now routes: 1 unrouted -> 0. Existing routing/determinism tests unchanged. Fuller routing exposed a separate GND-pour-island bug (new bead).

title: Access-aware assembly sequencing (spatial), beyond height heuristic
description: Current ordering is a good heuristic: back side first, then low-to-high by type (R,D,Q,U,C,SW,pots,jacks), panel hardware last. But true physical-access sequencing needs spatial reasoning — a placed tall part must not block iron/tweezer access to a shorter neighbour soldered later, and clearance between adjacent parts matters. Consider per-part height (from footprint courtyard/3D or a height table) + neighbour-proximity to refine order within a kind group. User feedback 2026-07-23.

title: Router: THT-aware layer transitions (no redundant vias on through-hole pads)
description: On a double-sided board the maze router drops a via essentially on top of a through-hole pad (DRC hole_to_hole warning: two drilled holes too close). A through-hole pad already connects both copper layers, so the router should treat reaching a Both-layer pad as a FREE layer transition and never place a via on/adjacent to one. Fix: mark through-hole pad cells as owned-by-net on BOTH layers (connection points on either side), and forbid via placement within a through-hole pad's keep-out. Exposed by the double_sided.py demo (SMD front + THT header back); currently a warning, not an error.
close_reason: Router now treats through-hole pads as free layer transitions (PadLayer::layers): a pad is a source/target on every layer it touches, so the router meets a through-hole pad on whichever side the net is already on instead of vias-ing onto its hole. double_sided.py hole_to_hole warnings 4->0; all boards 0 errors.

title: Reconcile back-side ground pour with back-side components (DESIGN 6.2)
description: The 'bottom = pure ground, no components' mental model earlier drafts implicitly carried is WRONG for Eurorack (stays true for THT-pedal single-sided). A solid ground pour on the back copper AND components mounted on that same physical side are NOT mutually exclusive: SMD parts sit on a mostly-ground-poured layer, routed around, with the pour knocked out around their pads/traces. Update the pour generation + routing so back-side components coexist with the back-copper GND pour. DESIGN says: worth a closer pass once double-sided placement logic is actually being built, not before — so this follows the side-aware placement work.
notes:
Considered as a design-rule variant (legion-of-bom-avg) and REJECTED, twice over:

1. What this bead actually asks for — a back-copper GND pour coexisting with back-side components, knocked out around their pads, plus via-stitching the pour to GND pads — is board GENERATION work on copper geometry produced after placement. The rule system evaluates placements. Forcing it in would be the wrong shape.

2. The placement-shaped version cannot fire. For the pour to flow between two parts the gap must exceed 2*clearance + min_thickness = 2(0.2) + 0.25 = 0.65mm, but the placer already enforces PLACE_CLEARANCE_MM = 1.5mm between keep-outs. The rule is satisfied by construction and would never report anything — which is the anti-pattern recorded on avg: a rule nobody can fail reads as a guarantee we never checked.

So this stays generation work. The tractable first slice is the concrete instance already in the notes: via-stitch the pour to GND pads, which fixes the isolated_copper warning when a GND net's only pad is on the opposite layer. Roughly the size of the power-header silkscreen work.

title: silkscreen_collision violation type in DRC-readback (DESIGN 6.10)
description: Add a silkscreen_collision violation type to the DRC-readback check step (6.5). Silkscreen-over-pad or silkscreen-over-silkscreen is NOT an electrical DRC violation, so it passes the existing copper/electrical check silently — the layout loop's check step must surface it explicitly. Depends on the silkscreen actually being generated (6.10 gen) and on the IPC DRC + violation readback plumbing (j54.11).
close_reason: DrcViolation::is_silkscreen_collision + DrcReport::silkscreen_collisions/count classify KiCad silk keys (silk_overlap/silk_over_copper) by 'silk' substring; CLI drc report surfaces them in a dedicated section with locations, separate from electrical warnings. Verified against a real colliding board (3 flagged) and clean boards (0). Not gated on is_clean (warnings, not electrical).

title: Silkscreen generation v0 — refdes/polarity/pin-1, KiCad defaults (DESIGN 6.10)
description: Silkscreen (reference designators, polarity marks, pin-1 indicators) is a distinct KiCad layer the sexp-gen/DRC copper work (6.6) never touched. v0 scope: ACCEPT KiCad's default reference-designator auto-placement rather than building custom placement logic — real auto-arrangement of silkscreen text to avoid overlaps is its own hard label-placement problem, not worth solving before a single real board ships. Ensure refdes + polarity marks + pin-1 indicators render on F.SilkS/B.SilkS in the generated .kicad_pcb. Matters directly (not cosmetic) for THT hand-assembly from a BOM: polarity marks in particular must be correct and visible — wrong-polarity assembly (diodes, electrolytics, ICs) is a common DIY failure mode. Feeds 7.8 build-guide rendering (the populated-board render needs accurate silkscreen, not just accurate copper). THT's low part count + 0.1in grid makes collisions rare, so defaults are a forgiving first cut.
close_reason: Silk (refdes+polarity+pin-1) renders via wholesale footprint placement; added Reference-unhide for guaranteed visibility + 2 regression tests. Front on F.SilkS, back mirrored to B.SilkS. DRC clean.

title: Compatible-substitute suggestions at BOM time (DESIGN 9.6)
description: Advisory only, NEVER automatic. At generate_bom time, if a primary MPN has low/zero stock, pull every part sharing its pin_compatible_groups entry and check each LIVE against the SUBCIRCUIT'S declared requires block (3.4) using the stored part_ratings (3.5) — not a hardcoded 'part X substitutes for Y' fact, which would ignore that the same swap can be fine in one role (buffer) and wrong in another (noise-sensitive signal path). Passing candidates are surfaced to the human for approval at BOM time; nothing swaps automatically. Depends on: pin_compatible_groups table, subcircuit role-requirements, okm part_ratings + verified gate, and a live stock signal (zya.2 Mouser).

title: pin_compatible_groups table (DESIGN 9.6)
description: A small, hand-maintained table of physically drop-in part families (op-amp pinout-compatible groups, etc.), each row (group_id, mpn, package, verified_by_human). This is the only genuinely stable fact worth caching — footprint/pinout compatibility doesn't change — so it's a cached relation, unlike the live requirement check. verified_by_human gated like the rest of the parts library (okm.4). Schema per DESIGN 9.6: CREATE TABLE pin_compatible_groups (group_id INT, mpn VARCHAR(64), package VARCHAR(32), verified_by_human BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE).

title: Layout: IPC DRC + violation readback via kicad-ipc-rs (loop check step)
description: What survives of the kicad-ipc-rs plan after de-risk: it's an EDITING/INSPECTION library (can't create boards / add footprints / assign nets — that's direct-gen's job now), but it CAN move existing footprints, run DRC, and read back violations against a board open in a running KiCad. That's exactly the layout loop's CHECK step (6.5 step 3): read DRC/critical-net violations to drive repairs. Requires KiCad running + IPC enabled (Preferences → Plugins). Targets KiCad 10.0.1. Optional for a first non-iterative board; needed for the iterative loop.
acceptance_criteria: connect to a running KiCad, run DRC on the open board, read back violations as structured data the layout loop consumes

CLI: lob drc <board> reports + exits non-zero on errors. This is the layout loop's check step (6.5 step 3). Surfaced a real latent issue (isolated GND pour -> j54.17 stitching).

title: Parts: license handling policy (metadata, not a pipeline gate)

See LIBRARIES.md.

title: layout: replace HPWL with Steiner-tree wirelength in the placement score
description:
layout::measure computes signal_hpwl_mm (half-perimeter wirelength) and score() weights it. The routability-driven placement literature is clear that Steiner-tree wirelength (StWL) correlates with actual routed wirelength substantially better than HPWL, and that wirelength alone does not capture local congestion at all — see the two estimation papers in [[legion-of-bom-REFS]].

DELIBERATELY DEFERRED. It improves the weakest term in the score, but that term is not currently causing trouble: since the tiered rules landed (legion-of-bom-avg), rule violations dominate attempt selection and HPWL only breaks ties. Worth doing when either (a) rule-clean boards start differing only by wirelength and the choices look wrong, or (b) we add congestion/routability to the score, at which point HPWL's blindness to congestion becomes the limiting factor.

Cheapest version: rectilinear minimum spanning tree as a Steiner approximation over each net's placed pads — no router involvement, same shape as the current per-net loop in measure().

title: refs: academic grounding for layout automation (constraint-driven, PCB placement, PDN)
description:
Verified 2026-07-26. Cite these rather than re-deriving; where marked ABSTRACT ONLY the body was not read (ACM DL 403).

CONSTRAINT-DRIVEN LAYOUT — the lineage crates/core/src/rules.rs sits in:
- Malavasi, Charbon, Felt, Sangiovanni-Vincentelli, 'Automation of IC layout with analog constraints', IEEE TCAD 15(8):923-941, 1996. Foundational formulation.
- Chang et al., 'A Top-Down, Constraint-Driven Design Methodology for Analog Integrated Circuits' (Berkeley). https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-1-4757-2233-8_13
- ALIGN: Dhar, Kunal, Li, Madhusudan, Poojary, Sharma, Xu, Burns, Harjani, Hu, Kirkpatrick, Mukherjee, Sapatnekar, Yaldiz. IEEE Design & Test 38(2):8-18, 2021. https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.10682 — derives constraints hierarchically FROM THE NETLIST rather than hand annotation, which is what decoupling_pairs does in miniature.
- MAGICAL: automatic constraint extraction from an unannotated netlist. https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/dc7241bb084c979aec6e1dd8cbf8f09b39fbc12b

PCB-SPECIFIC (closest to our problem; IC literature does not transfer cleanly):
- Liu, Agnesina, Ren, 'Challenges for Automating PCB Layout', ISPD 2024. https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3626184.3635285 — ABSTRACT ONLY.
- Tsou, Lin, Hung, Chang, 'Modern Automatic PCB Placement with Complex Constraints', DAC 2024. https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3649329.3663495 — ABSTRACT ONLY. Journal extension: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11195800/
- 'Constraint Graph-Based PCB Legalization Considering Dense, Heterogeneous, Irregular-Shaped, and Any-Oriented Components', DAC 2025. https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1109/DAC63849.2025.11133304 — irregular shapes and arbitrary orientation, i.e. exactly our rotated-header problem.
- 'An analytical approach and fine-tuning strategy for PCB placement optimization'. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S016792602500224X — the three-stage architecture (global -> legalization -> fine-tuning) we are missing a stage of.

PLACEMENT OBJECTIVE:
- 'Wirelength and congestion estimation for routability-driven placement' https://www.researchgate.net/publication/221031529
- 'Fast and Accurate Routing Demand Estimation' https://www.researchgate.net/publication/221339455
  Both: wirelength alone does not capture congestion; Steiner-tree WL correlates with routed WL far better than HPWL.

POWER INTEGRITY:
- Altium PDN decoupling: https://resources.altium.com/p/decoupling-strategies-for-pdn — proximity is a PROXY; the objective is loop inductance. A cap 2mm away with poor vias can beat one 5mm away with good vias.
- 'Hierarchical Decoupling Capacitor Optimization for PDN of 2.5D ICs', arXiv 2407.04737 — RL over frequency/time-domain co-analysis. Far beyond us, but confirms the objective is impedance, not millimetres.

title: DipTrace native import (.dch/.dip) — blocked on a proprietary binary format
description:
To get connectivity (a netlist, hence schematic/ERC/simulation) out of the SuperSynthesis modules, not just their layout, we would need the DipTrace source.

BLOCKER, verified: .dch and .dip are proprietary BINARY files — a .dch starts with magic \\x07DTSCHEM followed by length-prefixed UTF-16LE strings and undocumented records. There is no public spec. Reverse-engineering it is a large, fragile job that breaks on any DipTrace version bump.

BETTER PATHS, in order:
1. Export from DipTrace itself to an interchange format (it can write netlists, PADS/P-CAD/Eagle, Specctra DSN). Needs a DipTrace licence + a manual step per module, but is reliable and gives real connectivity. If the upstream project will publish an exported netlist alongside the binaries, that is the cheapest fix of all.
2. Recover connectivity from the gerbers by tracing copper and matching pads to the CPL. Doable in principle, genuinely hard, and produces nets with no names or intent.
3. Reverse-engineer the binary. Last resort.

Until one of those lands, [[legion-of-bom-u7p]] gets the layout, BOM and placement from the fab package, which covers re-use and ordering; only schematic/ERC/simulation are missing.

title: Parametric brand identity — curated brand kit (DESIGN 7.9)
description: Boards/panels should read as designed products, not raw pipeline output — even the fully-automatic ones. Same automatable/curated split as 7.8: (1) Automatable parametric layer — a small fixed set of house-style rules: consistent silkscreen typography, logo placement as a FUNCTION of panel dimensions (e.g. bottom-center, N% of panel width, M mm from edge) not a fixed pixel position, consistent border/frame, defined finish/color palette per product line — applied programmatically to every board via the same PanelSpec/silkscreen (6.10) path. (2) Stays manual/curated — illustration, one-off artwork, genuine creative choices. The risk this names: a system that INVENTS its own placement/spacing heuristics reads as generated no matter how correct; 'curated, not generated' comes from the rules being designed ONCE by a human and applied consistently, not from clever automation. Practical shape: a small brand kit (logo as scalable vector so it holds across HP widths / enclosure sizes, legend typography, the placement-rule set) stored ONCE as a shared asset referenced by every PanelSpec (Eurorack, Guitar Pedal, ...), not duplicated per product line. It's cross-project brand identity, so it likely belongs with the other shared/global concerns (parts library, panel-order tracking), not inside a per-circuit repo — storage mechanism (Dolt vs a brand/ dir in legion-of-bom) is an open detail, not resolved in DESIGN.
